fields.label: Root Soil Thickness
fields.help: Enter the thickness of the root-zone soil layer. Valid values are > 0. The default value is 0.80 minus the surface soil thickness. This is based on the summation of the default surface soil thickness when untilled and the U.S average root zone thickness from Table 16 of McKone et al. 2001 (Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models). See the TRIM User Guide Appendix for full reference information

fields.label: Air Content
fields.help: Enter the volume fraction of air in the soil layer (volumetric pore space occupied by air). Valid values are 0 to 1. The default value of 0.28 is the U.S. average in Table 15 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk. For wetland parcels, a value of 0.1 might be appropriate (professional judgment).

fields.label: Average Vertical Velocity of Water (Percolation)
fields.help: Enter the average downward velocity of water in the soil layer. Valid values are > 0. The default value is calculated based on the assumption of 0.2 multiplied by the average meters of daily precipitation for the modeled site. For wetland parcels, a value of 0 might be appropriate (professional judgment).

fields.label: Density of Soil Solids (Dry Weight)
fields.help: Enter the dry weight density of soil solids in the soil layer. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 2,600 is the value used by the CalTOX model (see Table 1 of: CalEPA (California Environmental Protection Agency), Department of Toxic Substances Control. 1996. The Distribution of California Landscape Variables for CalTOX. Draft (February). For wetland parcels, a value of 500 might be appropriate (professional judgment).

fields.label: Fraction Sand
fields.help: Enter the fraction of the soil layer that is sand. Valid values are 0 to 1. The default value of 0.25 is professional judgment. Typical sources of site-specific values include the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Web Soil Survey (Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Web Soil Survey. Available online at https://websoilsurvey.nrcs.usda.gov/.).

fields.label: Organic Carbon Fraction
fields.help: Enter the mass fraction of the soil solids which is made up of organic carbon in the soil layer. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 0.008 is the U.S. average in Table 16 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk. Typical sources of site-specific values include the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Web Soil Survey (Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Web Soil Survey. Available online at https://websoilsurvey.nrcs.usda.gov/.).

fields.label: pH
fields.help: Enter the pH of the soil layer. Valid values are 0 to 14. The default value of 6.8 is professional judgment. Typical sources of site-specific values include the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Web Soil Survey (Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Web Soil Survey. Available online at https://websoilsurvey.nrcs.usda.gov/.).

fields.label: Water Content
fields.help: Enter the volume fraction of water in the soil layer (volumetric pore space occupied by water). Valid values are 0 to 1. The default value of 0.19 is the U.S. average in Table 15 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk. Typical sources of site-specific values include the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Web Soil Survey (Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Web Soil Survey. Available online at https://websoilsurvey.nrcs.usda.gov/.). For wetland parcels, a value of 0.6 might be appropriate (professional judgment).
